Widen the central gap to produce a more legible public void and reduce collision across views.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the ambiguous split-wing macro with a clearer split-based dominant mass while preserving the linear datum.
Increase separation to make the public void and mass hierarchy more legible.
Keep a grounded connector so the split reads as one buildable figure rather than two colliding pieces.
Raise the base connector enough to strengthen the street threshold and create a clearer occupied ground band.
Calm the upper massing so the sectional gesture reads as a neighborhood building rather than a sculptural wedge.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant split-wing mass, but its visible organization is weakly aligned to the neighborhood-living brief. In the four views, the form is coherent enough to avoid total fragmentation, yet it leans toward a generic split and bend sequence rather than a clearly public ground threshold. The blue access edge is not met with a legible entry seam, court, or undercut; instead the mass mostly seals or glances past it. The top and opposite views suggest the two wings and bends are visually related, but the resulting figure does not convincingly produce usable public void or terrace logic in section. The silhouette is somewhat resolved, but the stepped/bent condition does not rise to a program-meaningful sectional move for this use. Compared with the references, it has some similarity to sectional/courtyard strategies, but it lacks the clear ground activation of the similar commercial precedents and especially the robust sectional public void logic of the counterfactual 8 House. Overall this is a plausible mass study, but not yet program-fit for neighborhood living.
